trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,-1); going right leaves no safe move afterwards (and 2 more options fail too). So the line goes left.
The line must go down-right: up-left is number 18, which comes later; up-right is number 19, which comes later; left is number 14, which comes later; down-left is number 7, which comes later.
Going down-left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,2). So the line goes right.
Going to number 3 leaves no safe move afterwards; going down-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going down-left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 5; going down-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 5. So the line goes down-right.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 5. So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-right.
The line must go up-left: left is number 10, which comes later.
Going left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 11. So the line goes down-left.
Number 9 is only reachable this way.
Going down-left would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going down-right would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going to number 12 would leave both cell (-3,0) and number 13 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-left.
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would turn number 13 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.

Going left would leave both cell (0,-3) and number 17 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-left would cut off the top-left corner (3 cells) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left would turn number 17 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 18. So the line goes down-right.
The only move that doesn't jump ahead to a later number (or break a rule) is up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 17 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 14/37 cells (38%).
Generation 1: fitness 21/37. The best line covers 24 cells, the first 21 of them still look solvable.
Generation 2: fitness 21/37. The best line covers 29 cells, the first 21 of them still look solvable.
Generation 3: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 3: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 120 futures: 92% survive going left (best covers 57%); right 83%; up-right 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 100% survive going right (best covers 57%); down-left 0%.
Tried 72 futures: 100% survive going up-right (best covers 57%); right 100%; down-right 100%.
Tried 48 futures: 96% survive going down-right (best covers 57%); up-left 0%.
Jackpot! A future covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 3,226 variables and 8,774 clauses in 0.01 s (884 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.02 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
